feature.title: Outlet Eligibility
feature.contentMd:
## What It Does
Determines which outlets are eligible for a specific promotion using configurable targeting criteria mapped to attributes like Outlet Type, Channel, Key Account, Segment, etc.

The same targeting mechanism handles both outlet and product attributes — targeting criteria are configurable per tenant.

## Common Questions
- **How do I target specific shops or outlets for a promotion?** Use outlet targeting criteria — select the attributes (Outlet Type, Channel, Segment, Key Account, etc.) that define which outlets should receive the promo.
- **Can I target only Gold-tier or Premium outlets?** Yes — set Outlet Type = Gold or Segment = Premium in the targeting criteria.
- **Can I set different promo dates for different outlets?** Yes — use Outlet Bifurcations (per-outlet date overrides). Each outlet can have its own activation/deactivation date within the promo period.
- **Can I target a manually curated list of outlets?** Yes — use Named Outlet Groups to maintain a custom list like 'Top 100 Outlets'.

## How It Works
Each tenant can configure up to 20 targeting criteria, each mapped to a attribute. When creating a promotion, the user selects values for the criteria that matter (e.g., Outlet Type = Gold, Channel = Modern Trade). All unselected criteria default to 'all' (no restriction).

When an order comes in, the system checks the outlet's attributes against the promo's criteria. ALL selected criteria must match (AND logic).

## Rules
1. Up to 20 configurable targeting criteria per tenant, each mapped to a attribute
2. Users see labels (Outlet Type, Channel) — not technical names
3. Typically 5-6 criteria used per tenant
4. Setting a criterion to 'all' means no restriction on that attribute
5. Named Outlet Groups: manually maintained groups (e.g., Top 100 Outlets)
6. Outlet Bifurcations: per-outlet date overrides for active/inactive windows

## Data & Fields
| Field | Description | Required | Example |
|-------|-------------|----------|--------|
| Outlet Type | Classification | No | Gold / Silver / Bronze |
| Channel | Distribution channel | No | Modern Trade / General Trade |
| Key Account | Named group | No | Reliance Retail |
| Segment | Market segment | No | Premium / Value |
| Outlet Group | Manually maintained group | No | Top 100 Outlets |
| Outlet Start Date | Per-outlet activation | No | 2024-06-15 |
| Outlet End Date | Per-outlet deactivation | No | 2024-07-15 |

## Tenant-Level Configurations
| Config Point | Options | Default | Example |
|-------------|---------|---------|--------|
| Outlet attribute targeting | Maps attributes to targeting criteria | Tenant-specific | OutletType, Channel |
| Active targeting criteria | 1-20 | 10 | Most tenants use 5-6 |
| Outlet group targeting | ON/OFF | OFF | Enable custom groups |

scenarios.title: Configuring Outlet Filters for a Promotion
scenarios.contentMd:
## Common Questions
- **How do multiple outlet criteria work together?** All criteria use AND logic — the outlet must match ALL selected criteria.
- **What if I select multiple values for one criterion (e.g., Gold AND Silver)?** Multiple values within the same criterion use OR logic — Gold OR Silver outlets match.

## Example
A company wants to run a 'Premium Channel Push' promo targeting Gold-tier outlets in Modern Trade:

1. Trade marketing opens promo creation in UI
2. Sees outlet targeting section with labeled dropdowns: Outlet Type, Channel, Key Account, Segment, Sub-Channel, Region
3. Selects **Outlet Type = Gold** and **Channel = Modern Trade**
4. Leaves all other criteria on 'all' (no restriction)
5. Saves the promotion

Now, when orders come in:
- A Gold outlet in Modern Trade places an order → **promo IS applied** ✓
- A Gold outlet in General Trade places an order → **promo is NOT applied** ✗ (Channel doesn't match)
- A Silver outlet in Modern Trade places an order → **promo is NOT applied** ✗ (Outlet Type doesn't match)

## Example with Multiple Values
A promo targets Outlet Type = Gold OR Silver (both values selected for the same criterion):
- Gold outlet → ✓ matches
- Silver outlet → ✓ matches
- Bronze outlet → ✗ does not match

Multiple values within the same criterion use OR logic. Different criteria use AND logic.

## Rules
1. Each targeting criterion maps to a attribute via tenant configuration
2. Selecting 'all' for a criterion = no restriction on that dimension
3. Criteria combine with AND logic: all selected criteria must match
4. When multiple values are selected for one criterion, the system validates targeting before saving

scenarios.title: Outlet Groups and Per-Outlet Date Overrides
scenarios.contentMd:
## Common Questions
- **Can I target a specific list of outlets instead of using attributes?** Yes — create a Named Outlet Group (e.g., 'Top 100 Outlets') and target the group.
- **Can I set custom start/end dates for individual outlets within a promo?** Yes — use Outlet Bifurcations. Each outlet can have its own activation window.

## Example — Named Outlet Groups
A company has a special 'Top 100 Outlets' group curated by the sales team:
1. The sales team maintains a list of 100 high-performing outlets across all channels
2. Trade marketing creates a promo targeting 'Top 100 Outlets' group
3. Only outlets in this specific group will receive the promo — regardless of their type, channel, or segment
4. When a new outlet is added to or removed from the group, the promo eligibility updates automatically

## Example — Outlet Bifurcations (Per-Outlet Date Overrides)
A promo runs from Jan 1 to Mar 31, but some outlets need different activation dates:
1. Promo 'Q1 Push' is active Jan 1 - Mar 31
2. Outlet #123 (new outlet, opened Feb 1) gets a bifurcation: active from Feb 1 only
3. Outlet #456 (seasonal outlet) gets a bifurcation: active only Jan 15 - Feb 28
4. All other outlets follow the main promo dates (Jan 1 - Mar 31)

Bifurcations allow per-outlet customization of the promo window without creating separate promotions.

## Rules
1. Outlet groups are manually maintained lists of outlet codes
2. A promo can target outlet groups independently of attribute-based targeting
3. Bifurcations override the promo start/end date for specific outlets
4. Bifurcation dates must fall within the overall promo period
5. Groups are updated by the sales or trade marketing team
